questions.q: What are the main components created when a node starts in KRaft mode as a controller, and how do they depend on each other?
facts: KafkaRaftServer creates one SharedServer and, based on process.roles, a ControllerServer and/or a BrokerServer; the controller is started before the broker
SharedServer owns the pieces shared by broker and controller (the Raft manager, the metadata loader and the snapshot generator), with a single instance even in combined mode

KafkaRaftManager builds the metadata RaftLog, the KafkaNetworkChannel, the KafkaRaftClient and a KafkaRaftClientDriver that runs it; its startup() initializes the client with the voters and a FileQuorumStateStore
ControllerServer builds the QuorumController on top of raftManager.client (the QuorumController itself is outside this excerpt)

questions.q: What happens, in order, when the controller part of a node starts up, up to the point where it serves requests?
facts: It creates the SocketServer, builds ListenerInfo from the advertised controller listeners, and calls sharedServer.startForController(listenerInfo), which starts the shared Raft manager before any QuorumController exists
It waits (bounded by the startup deadline) for controllerQuorumVotersFuture, then builds the QuorumController
It creates ControllerApis and a request handler pool, collects the metadata publishers, and waits for sharedServer.loader.installPublishers(metadataPublishers)
It then enables request processing on the SocketServer, starts the registration channel manager and the ControllerRegistrationManager, and waits for the authorizer futures and the socket acceptors
Any Throwable during startup goes to sharedServer.controllerStartupFaultHandler, then shutdown() runs and the exception is rethrown

questions.q: What happens end to end when a new controller node automatically joins an existing quorum as a voter?
facts: The new node runs as an observer following the leader; pollFollowerAsObserver sends AddRaftVoter only when kraft.version supports reconfiguration, canBecomeVoter is true (process.roles includes controller), quorumConfig.autoJoin() is set, and the update-voter-set period has expired
If the node's id is already in the voter set under a different directory id, it sends RemoveRaftVoter for that old voter key instead of AddRaftVoter
The leader's AddVoterHandler sends an API_VERSIONS request to the new node and stores the pending operation as an AddVoterHandlerState; the AddVoter response future completes later

When the API_VERSIONS reply passes validation, the leader adds the node to lastVoterSet() and appends the new VotersRecord via LeaderState.appendVotersRecord; if ackWhenCommitted is false the success response is sent immediately

The pending operation is cleared in AddVoterHandler.highWatermarkUpdated once the high watermark passes the VotersRecord's offset, which is also when an ackWhenCommitted request gets its success response

questions.q: When the leader receives a request to add a voter, what does it check before accepting it, and what error does each failed check return?
facts: KafkaRaftClient.handleAddVoterRequest calls validateLeaderOnlyRequest with the node's own quorum.epoch() (the request carries no epoch), so the only leader-level rejections are NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER and BROKER_NOT_AVAILABLE (shutting down)
A voter key without a directory id, or listeners without an endpoint for the default listener, is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST

AddVoterHandler returns REQUEST_TIMED_OUT when another voter change is pending, when the high watermark is not yet established, or when the latest VotersRecord is not committed (its offset >= HWM) or there is no VotersRecord in the log at all
It returns UNSUPPORTED_VERSION when kraft.version does not support reconfiguration, and DUPLICATE_VOTER when the id is already in the voter set

questions.q: Where is the set of quorum voters kept, what does each voter entry contain, and where does it come from at startup?
facts: VoterSet maps voter id to a VoterNode holding a ReplicaKey voterKey (id plus optional directory id), the voter's listener Endpoints, and its supported kraft.version range
VoterSet is immutable: addVoter (and removeVoter/updateVoter) return a new VoterSet in an Optional, which is empty if the change is not allowed (e.g. the id already exists)
Statically configured voters become a VoterSet via fromInetSocketAddresses, with Uuid.ZERO_UUID as the directory id and a supported kraft.version range of (0, 0)

KafkaRaftClient.initialize hands that static set to KRaftControlRecordStateMachine (partitionState), which reads the snapshot and log; the live voter set is then read through partitionState.lastVoterSet()

questions.q: Where does a node persist its election state (epoch, leader, who it voted for) so it survives a restart, and when is it written?
facts: QuorumState.durableTransitionTo calls store.writeElectionState(newState.election(), partitionState.lastKraftVersion()) before memoryTransitionTo swaps in the new state
The store is a FileQuorumStateStore in the Raft manager's data directory, created in KafkaRaftManager.startup and passed to KafkaRaftClient.initialize
transitionToResigned uses memoryTransitionTo only: Resigned is a soft state that is not persisted
On restart, a node whose stored election shows it as leader comes back as Resigned in the same epoch; if the stored epoch is behind the log's last epoch it starts Unattached at the log's epoch

questions.q: Where is the code that decides whether this node grants its vote to a candidate?
facts: KafkaRaftClient.handleVoteRequest validates the request, then calls quorum.canGrantVote(replicaKey, isLogUpToDate, preVote), where isLogUpToDate compares the candidate's last offset and epoch with the local log end
A Vote request with a higher epoch first transitions the node to Unattached in that epoch
QuorumState.canGrantVote delegates to the current EpochState; LeaderState.canGrantVote always returns false

The shared rule for Unattached and Prospective replicas, QuorumState.unattachedOrProspectiveCanGrantVote, grants a PreVote whenever the log is up to date, but grants a real vote only if the node has not voted for a different candidate, knows no leader in that epoch, and the candidate's log is up to date
A granted real (non-pre) vote is recorded durably through unattachedAddVotedState or prospectiveAddVotedState

questions.q: Where is the code that decides what counts as committed (the high watermark), and what makes it move?
facts: LeaderState.maybeUpdateHighWatermark sorts the voters by descending end offset and takes the offset at index voterStates.size() / 2; the leader counts as one of the voters

The high watermark only advances once that offset is past epochStartOffset, i.e. after a record from the leader's own epoch is replicated, which is why onBecomeLeader immediately appends start-of-epoch control records
It is recomputed when a replica fetches (updateReplicaState, called from tryCompleteFetchRequest) and when the leader's own end offset changes (updateLocalState); fetches from observers never move it
When it moves, onUpdateLeaderHighWatermark notifies the add, remove and update voter handlers, completes the append and fetch purgatories, and delivers newly committed data to listeners

questions.q: Which types represent a node's role in the election (leader, follower, candidate, ...), and who is allowed to change it?
facts: Each role is its own EpochState class: UnattachedState, ProspectiveState, CandidateState, LeaderState, FollowerState and ResignedState; Prospective and Candidate are both NomineeStates
QuorumState holds the current role in its volatile `state` field and owns every transition (the transitionToX methods), following the transition table in its class comment
Observers (non-voters) only ever move between Unattached and Follower
KafkaRaftClient.pollCurrentState dispatches on the current role to pollLeader, pollCandidate, pollProspective, pollFollower, pollUnattached or pollResigned

questions.q: Where is the code that makes a leader give up leadership, and what happens to the node afterwards?
facts: pollLeader resigns when a graceful shutdown is in progress, when a resignation was requested, or when the check-quorum timer has expired
The check-quorum timer is reset only after a majority of voters have fetched during the interval (the leader counts implicitly), in updateCheckQuorumForFollowingVoter
Resigning fails all parked fetches with NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER, and the preferred successors are the non-leader voters ordered by descending fetch offset
In the Resigned state, pollResigned sends EndQuorumEpoch to voters that have not acknowledged, and after the election timeout (unless shutting down) moves to Unattached at epoch + 1

questions.q: If I change VoterSet (for example how isVoter or voterIds behave), what else is affected?
facts: QuorumState.isVoter() and isObserver() come from partitionState.lastVoterSet().isVoter(ReplicaKey(localId, localDirectoryId)), which decides whether this node behaves as a voter or an observer
LeaderState.updateVoterAndObserverStates rebuilds the leader's voterStates from the latest VoterSet and moves voters that are no longer in it into observerStates
AddVoterHandler's DUPLICATE_VOTER check uses voterIds()
Election requests look up their destinations with voterNode(id, listenerName) and throw IllegalStateException when a voter has no endpoint for the listener

questions.q: If I change SharedServer's start/stop logic, what else is affected?
facts: Both ControllerServer (startForController) and BrokerServer (startForBroker) start it; it really starts only for the first caller, tracked with the usedByController / usedByBroker flags

The Raft manager starts with the first caller's endpoints: the controller listener endpoints from startForController, Endpoints.empty() from startForBroker, which is why KafkaRaftServer starts the controller before the broker
KafkaRaftServer shuts the broker down before the controller, because controller shutdown stops the Raft client early
ControllerServer.shutdown calls sharedServer.ensureNotRaftLeader(), which shuts down and nulls the whole RaftManager because there is no resign API

questions.q: How would I add handling for a new Raft RPC type in the raft client?
facts: Inbound requests are dispatched on the Raft poll thread by the switch on ApiKeys in KafkaRaftClient.handleRequest; add a case returning a CompletionStage of the response
If that stage completes exceptionally, the reply is built with RaftUtil.errorResponse(apiKey, ...)
Responses to requests this node sent are dispatched by the switch in handleResponse; the boolean result goes to requestManager.onResponseResult (false means back off)
Leader-only APIs validate with validateLeaderOnlyRequest (FENCED_LEADER_EPOCH, UNKNOWN_LEADER_EPOCH, NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER, BROKER_NOT_AVAILABLE)

Outbound requests go through maybeSendRequest, which respects requestManager backoff and readiness and routes the response back through messageQueue; on the server side, KafkaRaftManager.handleRequest just forwards to KafkaRaftClientDriver.handleRequest

questions.q: How would I add a new component on the controller that reacts to metadata changes?
facts: Implement a MetadataPublisher, as ControllerRegistrationManager does: onMetadataUpdate(delta, newImage, manifest) receives each change and close() shuts it down
In ControllerServer.startup, add the instance to metadataPublishers before sharedServer.loader.installPublishers(metadataPublishers) is awaited
The existing controller publishers take sharedServer.metadataPublishingFaultHandler, which is non-fatal and only increments error metrics
Order in the list can matter: the startup code requires config.dynamicConfig.addReconfigurables(this) to run before DynamicClientQuotaPublisher is added
Publishers receive no metadata until the controller has caught up to the high watermark

questions.q: How are faults handled on a controller node? Which ones kill the process and which are only logged?
facts: SharedServer creates every fault handler through FaultHandlerFactory.build(name, fatal, action); StandardFaultHandlerFactory returns a ProcessTerminatingFaultHandler when fatal and a LoggingFaultHandler otherwise
Fatal: the raft manager, controller startup, initial broker metadata loading and QuorumController fatal faults; metadata loading is fatal only when the node has the controller role
Non-fatal: metadata publishing and non-fatal QuorumController faults, whose actions only increment error metrics

The metadata-loading, controller-startup, initial-broker-load and fatal QuorumController actions also disable snapshot generation by setting snapshotsDisabledReason; the raft manager handler's action is a no-op, and publishing faults explicitly do not disable snapshots
ControllerServer.startup catches any Throwable, calls controllerStartupFaultHandler.handleFault, runs shutdown() and rethrows

questions.q: How does a controller register itself with the cluster, and when does it consider itself registered?
facts: ControllerServer starts the ControllerRegistrationManager, with a NodeToControllerChannelManager built from RaftControllerNodeProvider, only after the socket server's request processing has been enabled

maybeSendControllerRegistration sends only when the node is not already registered, the channel manager is set, the metadata.version is known and supports controller registration, and no RPC is pending
The ControllerRegistrationRequest carries the controller id, the incarnation id, supported features and listeners, with zkMigrationReady false
A successful RPC response does not mark the node registered; registeredInLog becomes true only when a metadata update shows a registration for this node id with the same incarnation id
Error responses and timeouts reschedule the attempt with exponential backoff (scheduleNextCommunicationAfterFailure)
